record_id.rationale: No stable key. Contract reference number repeats across suppliers (109843 x17, HSQ84570 x8), has typos and placeholders ('TBC', 'HSQ109250 -4'), and sometimes holds several references in one cell. Even reference + supplier + dates can collide: Becton Dickinson HSQ102882-1 appears twice with different award dates. A hash of the full row is deterministic and traces back to one physical record.

values: Refer to Queensland Government Arrangements Directory

mappings.rationale: About 80% of values carry Pty Ltd/Limited/Inc style suffixes, so these are mostly registered names. The placeholder is nulled, and a trailing '(Trading As ...)' is cut off so only the registered part is kept. Some values have no company suffix (e.g. 'Kerr Australia', 'Switch Transformation Consultancy'), so those may be trading names or sole traders and the confidence is held down.

Only explicit '(Trading As X)' / '(t/as X)' text is taken as a trading name. Rows without it produce no value. Other bracketed text such as '(Qscan)' or '(I-Med)' is deliberately not mapped, because it cannot be told apart from '(Australia)' with the available transforms.

Spaced 11-digit ABNs. Digits are extracted, anything that is not exactly 11 digits (multi-ABN cells, 12-digit typos) gives no value, and the real ABN checksum is then enforced. Cells that fail the checksum (about 7% in the holdout) are dropped, not emitted.

values: Refer to Queensland Government Arrangements Directory

mappings.rationale: Free-text street address of the supplier. The placeholder is nulled. Embedded newlines are collapsed. A few cells hold two addresses separated by ';', which are kept as one string and flagged in the notes.

Takes the state token immediately before a trailing 4-digit postcode. It only matches a recognised AU state name or abbreviation (case-insensitive), then normalises it. Multi-address cells (containing ';'), placeholders, blanks and non-AU addresses give no value instead of a guess.

Takes the 4-digit postcode only when it directly follows an AU state token. This keeps NZ and overseas codes out of an AU field, and multi-address cells are excluded so one address's postcode is not attributed to the other.

source_reliability.rationale: Official agency disclosure register under CC-BY-4.0. Supplier names and ABNs are mostly well-formed, but entry is manual: typos (e.g. 'Austalia'), about 7-8% of ABNs fail checksum, placeholder suppliers, and several rows pack multiple suppliers into one cell.

notes: Revision v2: transform arguments are now at the top level of each transform object (the engine raised KeyError: 'pattern' when they were nested under 'args'). The ABN chain now routes non-11-digit cells to no value before the checksum.

The preview for legal_name, trading_name, address.state and address.postcode errored in the first run, so none of those four mappings has yet been checked against real output. Please check them on the next report.

ABN: the remaining checksum failures (about 4-5 of 86 in the holdout, e.g. 86 087 097 717, 96 126 888 259, 34 161 464 441) are genuine invalid ABNs in the source. They are dropped on purpose. The error rate sits close to the 0.05 threshold because of source data quality, not the mapping.
Parse with a quote-aware CSV reader. Quoted cells contain embedded newlines, including in Supplier address, Contract reference number and Variation comments.
Check the raw bytes for encoding (U+FFFD seen in free-text columns). Only free-text columns are affected. The mapped columns are ASCII in the samples.

About 10% of rows have the placeholder 'Refer to Queensland Government Arrangements Directory' as the supplier. They get no legal_name and usually no ABN or address, so they will carry few or no entity claims.

Multi-supplier rows exist (e.g. Elite Nursing Professionals row with two ABNs, two addresses and two contract refs, with one name). The ABN is skipped, and state and postcode are skipped. address.full is kept as one string containing both addresses. Please review these rows. A later version may need row-level splitting.
Some legal_name values have no company suffix (e.g. 'Kerr Australia'). They may be trading names, which is why legal_name confidence is 0.7.
Names such as 'X PTY LTD as Trustee for The Y Family Trust' come through as legal_name with the trust part included. A trustee relationship would be better modelled once the engine can extract it.
legal_name is source-as-stated, including typos (e.g. 'ICU Medical Austalia Pty Ltd'). Do not correct at ingest.
The same supplier appears on many rows (e.g. Slade Health x12). This yields many observations per entity, which is expected and left to reconciliation.

Dates, contract value and contract reference are deliberately not mapped, so this config emits entity and address claims only. If valid_from/valid_to are wanted for 'supplier on contract' claims, that should be a separate relationship or contract observation type, not an attribute validity window.
